options: A setting that only exists on the report server, never in the report itself
A column in the underlying database table
A named input a report reader supplies to control what the report shows, appearing on the report viewer toolbar
A type of chart used to visualize filtered data
questions.explain: A report parameter is the reader-facing input — a store, date range, or region — that shows up as a prompt on the report viewer toolbar.

questions.q: What happens automatically when you add a query variable like @StoreID to a dataset's query text?
options: The query stops running until you publish the report
Report Builder creates a matching dataset parameter and report parameter with the same name
Nothing — you must manually create both by hand every time
The report deletes all existing parameters
questions.explain: A query variable inside a dataset's query text automatically creates a matching dataset parameter and a report parameter to go with it — you don't have to build either by hand.

questions.q: Where do all of a report's parameters live in the design environment?
options: In a separate file outside the report entirely
Inside the Data Sources dialog only
Under the Parameters node in the Report Data pane
Only visible after the report is published to a Report Server
questions.explain: Every report parameter — automatic or manually added — appears under the Parameters node in the Report Data pane, alongside Built-in Fields, Data Sources, and Datasets.

questions.q: A query variable auto-creates a report parameter with data type Text, but the underlying column is really numeric. What's the typical fix?
options: Open Report Parameter Properties and change the Data type to Integer (or the appropriate numeric type)
Leave it as Text — data type never affects report behavior
Rename the query variable to fix the data type automatically
Delete the parameter and rebuild the entire dataset from scratch
questions.explain: Changing the Data type on the General tab of Report Parameter Properties is one of the most common first edits after Report Builder auto-creates a parameter as Text.

questions.q: Why would you set a parameter to Hidden instead of Visible?
options: Visible parameters cannot have default values
Hidden parameters run faster than visible ones
Hidden is required for every parameter with a Boolean data type
When its value is supplied by something else, like a drillthrough from another report, rather than typed by a person
questions.explain: Hidden parameters are common when a value arrives from elsewhere — like a drillthrough action passing a value — so there's no need to prompt a person for it on the toolbar.
